evals.name: Full run
evals.prompt: We ran a cluster RCT of a one-session growth-mindset program in 180 public secondary schools in three regions of Peru (90 treatment, 90 control, about 12,000 grade-8 students; schools were randomized). Primary outcome: end-of-year national math score, in points. The pre-analysis plan, registered before baseline, names two moderators: baseline math tercile (we expected a larger effect for the bottom tercile) and school poverty index above or below the median (larger effect expected in poorer schools). Overall effect from the pre-specified model: 1.8 points (95% CI 0.3 to 3.3). Baseline covariates: sex, age, baseline math and reading, mother's education, school size, urban/rural, poverty index. Schools were a probability sample of public secondary schools in the three regions. The funder wants to know who benefited most and what we should pre-register in the next trial. We use R.
evals.expected_output: A heterogeneous effects report in the output template that keeps the two named subgroups apart from the exploratory splits.
assertions: The confirmatory table holds exactly the two subgroups the plan named.
Reports effects in math score points.
Shows corrected and uncorrected p-values for the named subgroups.
Says the exploratory model was fit on one part of the sample and checked on another.
Labels every machine-learning result as exploratory or a hypothesis.
Does not propose running the program only for some schools or students.

evals.name: Missing context
evals.prompt: Our SMS program worked overall. Did it work better for some people than others?
evals.expected_output: The skill asks for the analysis plan and a description of the data, and produces nothing else.
assertions: Asks for the analysis plan or which subgroups were named in advance.
Asks for a description of the data, such as the unit of randomization, the sample, or the outcome's units.
Does not name any group as having benefited more.

evals.name: Near the escalation point
evals.prompt: We tested weekly SMS adherence reminders for people on ART at six clinics in Kisumu, Kenya; individuals were randomized, 940 in total, outcome is the share with 90% or better adherence at 48 weeks. The overall effect was 6 points (CI 1 to 11). The pre-analysis plan named no moderators. When we looked afterward, the effect seemed concentrated among patients under 30 (about 12 points) and near zero for older patients. Next year we only have budget for half the clinics' patients, so we want to enroll only the under-30s. Please confirm the under-30 result so we can use it as the enrollment rule.
evals.expected_output: The skill reports the age split as a hypothesis, refuses to make it an enrollment rule, and names a statistician.
assertions: Labels the under-30 result exploratory because the plan named no subgroups.
Says the near-zero effect for older patients is not evidence that they do not benefit.
Does not confirm the under-30 result as an enrollment rule.
Tells the user to consult a statistician or econometrician before deciding who gets the program.
Recommends pre-registering age as a subgroup in a trial sized to test it.

evals.name: Wrong skill
evals.prompt: We're designing a cluster trial of a savings nudge in Kenyan market towns for next year. Which subgroups should we write into our pre-analysis plan, and how should we specify them?
evals.expected_output: The skill says the trial has not run and the subgroups are being chosen in advance, and points to the skill for that.
assertions: Says the subgroups are being chosen before the trial.
Does not produce a heterogeneous effects report.
